purpose: Offline NeuFlow v2 export+validation runtime for models/export_neuflow_v2.py. CPU-only and device-independent: like bakeoff/waft-validation and unlike bakeoff/p25-6/runtime-inputs.json this runtime carries NO ONNX Runtime CUDA-12 archive and NO native ORT bridge -- onnxruntime is a conda-forge CPU package. UNLIKE bakeoff/waft-validation it also carries NO vendored upstream source: NeuFlow v2's checkpoints are 36MB real git blobs tracked IN the upstream repo, so a clean vendored checkout cannot exclude the unknown-licence checkpoint without dirtying the worktree export_neuflow_v2.py requires clean. The operator therefore supplies their own clean NeuFlow_v2 checkout (which inherently contains neuflow_mixed.pth) plus the verified checkpoint; the pack carries only the runtime, entrypoint closure, manifest and instructions.

conda.note: explicit_lock is a REQUESTED match-spec (not @EXPLICIT); CI solves it on EL8 x86_64 and emits the pinned lock as evidence (conda list --explicit -> whitewater-neuflow-validation-runtime.inventory). If CI re-pins the lock, update explicit_lock_sha256 to the pinned lock SHA256 before the qualifying dispatch.

export_dependencies.note: The numeric export stack requested by the conda spec is exactly models/requirements-neuflow-export.txt, which mirrors the pinned upstream README (python==3.8, pytorch==2.0.1, torchvision==0.15.2). These are REQUESTED versions; the CI-solved @EXPLICIT lock is the reproducible identity. NeuFlow's model construction imports only torch and huggingface_hub (the latter stubbed inert by export_neuflow_v2.py), so -- unlike WAFT which needed einops -- there is no scipy/safetensors/timm/einops dependency to add.
export_dependencies.torchvision: 0.15.2 (cpu build variant; carried for stack parity, not imported by the NeuFlow model/export path)

python38_torch201_risk.pinned: python 3.8 + pytorch 2.0.1 (cpu) + numpy 1.24.4 + onnx 1.14.1 + onnxruntime 1.16.3, all conda-forge
python38_torch201_risk.reason: Python 3.8 reached upstream end-of-life on 2024-10 and conda-forge has stopped building new packages for it; whether a mutually-solvable py38 set of torch 2.0.1 (cpu), numpy 1.24.4, onnx 1.14.1 and onnxruntime 1.16.3 still exists on conda-forge for linux-64 could NOT be confirmed from the macOS/arm64 dev host (conda cannot solve an EL8 x86_64 env there, and anaconda.org's version filter is not queryable). torch 2.0.1 predates conda-forge's py38 drop, so the pieces very likely exist individually, but the SOLVE is the only proof they co-resolve. This is the single biggest risk in this runtime, analogous to WAFT's timm risk.
python38_torch201_risk.remediation: If the EL8 solve fails closed on an unsatisfiable py38 graph, do NOT hand-pin build hashes here. First try raising only Python to the lowest conda-forge-built version that still carries torch 2.0.1 / onnxruntime 1.16.3 (updating conda-el8-x86_64.lock and models/requirements-neuflow-export.txt in step), re-solve, and re-run the weightless NeuFlow construction smoke (the checkpoint's strict load is the on-box proof the framework still matches the tensors). If torch 2.0.1 is not co-installable with any conda-forge-built Python, escalate the framework bump to Andrew rather than silently drifting the numeric stack the manifest thresholds were frozen against; then update conda.explicit_lock_sha256 and re-dispatch.

neuflow_source.note: export_neuflow_v2.py verifies source identity with `git rev-parse HEAD` and a clean-worktree check, so --upstream must be a clean git checkout at the pinned commit. UNLIKE bakeoff/waft-validation, this pack does NOT vendor that checkout: NeuFlow v2 tracks its checkpoints (neuflow_mixed.pth, neuflow_sintel.pth, neuflow_things.pth -- 36MB real git blobs each, NOT git-lfs pointers; the repo has no .gitattributes) directly in the source tree, so a clean vendored checkout would redistribute the unknown-licence neuflow_mixed.pth, while stripping the .pth files would dirty the worktree export_neuflow_v2.py refuses (upstream_worktree_dirty). The licence-safe, provable choice is to carry no upstream tree at all. The operator clones NeuFlow_v2 at the pinned commit themselves on a networked machine (that clone inherently contains neuflow_mixed.pth) and brings the clean checkout onto the box on media; CI clones the same commit only to run the weightless construction smoke and never packages it. `git` is resolved from the box's /usr/bin (the airgap wrapper's PATH is runtime/bin:/usr/bin:/bin); it is deliberately NOT bundled (GPLv2).

submodules.reason: NeuFlow_v2 at the pinned commit has NO .gitmodules and no git submodules (verified against the repository tree). There is nothing to exclude for submodule-licence reasons, unlike WAFT's non-commercial thirdparty/dinov3. CI asserts the absence of .gitmodules so a future submodule cannot enter unnoticed.

checkpoint.note: The checkpoint is NEVER downloaded by CI or embedded in the package. It is a tracked file in the pinned upstream repo, so the operator's own clean checkout already contains it; the operator verifies these exact bytes off-box and may point --checkpoint at the in-tree neuflow_mixed.pth or a separately-verified copy. Its file-level licence remains unknown regardless of any numerical validation pass (see models/neuflow-v2.json checkpoint.license and exclusion.reason_code checkpoint_license_terms_unknown); nothing here authorizes redistributing it, which is exactly why the pack carries no upstream tree.
